title: Are Canadian conservatives ditching the fringe?
summary: The B.C. Conservatives were falling apart just last month. Then they united and won the election in a landslide. What happened? And what can other conservative parties learn?

image.caption: B.C. Conservative interim Leader Lorne Doerkson celebrates on stage during provincial election night in Vancouver, on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026.THE CANADIAN PRESS/Ethan Cairns (THE CANADIAN PRESS)

blocks.text: The B.C. Conservatives were falling apart just last month. Then they united and won the election in a landslide. What happened? And what can other conservative parties learn?
Front Burner26:15Are Canadian conservatives ditching the fringe?

At the end of September the B.C. Conservative party had imploded. Today, they are set to run the province. It's a stunning reversal of political fortune for a party that had been torn apart by infighting and resignations before a snap election call by the NDP.

The whole situation raises a tonne of interesting questions. Was this a triumph of one particular brand of conservatism over another? Or just a rejection of the NDP? Are there lessons here for Danielle Smith in Alberta and the struggling federal Conservatives?
Political strategist Kory Teneycke, co-founder and CEO of Rubicon Strategy joins us to talk about it.
